entry.title: GIFT – “Every Step”
entry.summary: New York psych-pop quintet GIFT returning early next year with their new album 'Frenzy For The Thrill.' Listen to new single "Every Step."
entry.content:
GIFT, the New York psych-pop quintet and 2024 Band To Watch led by TJ Freda, are returning early next year with their new album Frenzy For The Thrill. Following the hard-hitting lead single "Hand To The Flame," they're easing up on the gas with the beautifully shimmering space-rock float of new track "Every Step." According to Freda:

Everything comes down to perspective. There's so much happening in the world that matters more than the small things we let upset us. But when those small things feel just as big, guilt comes along with them, and it's easy to feel disillusioned with yourself for not feeling the way you think you should. Perspective follows every step, whether you lean toward hope or toward heaviness. Beauty lives in the broken places, and something broken lives in every beautiful thing.

Listen and watch the accompanying music video, which shows a beaten-up Freda traveling through the city in search of a moment of peace, below.

Frenzy For The Thrill is out 1/15 on Captured Tracks. Pre-order it here.

entry.title: Christine And The Queens – “Rendez-vous Avec Toi”
entry.summary: It’s the start of a new era for Christine And The Queens. This year Rahim Redcar has been doing collabs with Logic1000, Thee Diane, and more, but now he’s back with “Rendez-vous Avec Toi,” the first taste of an upcoming album. The last Christine And The Queens LP was 2023’s PARANOÏA, ANGELS, TRUE LOVE, and…
entry.content:
It's the start of a new era for Christine And The Queens. This year Rahim Redcar has been doing collabs with Logic1000, Thee Diane, and more, but now he's back with "Rendez-vous Avec Toi," the first taste of an upcoming album.

The last Christine And The Queens LP was 2023's PARANOÏA, ANGELS, TRUE LOVE, and the followup is arriving next spring. "Rendez-vous Avec Toi" comes alongside "Rendez-vous In Your Arms," which is an English version of the same song. About the new single, Redcar says:

I have a rendez-vous with you, tonight 
I have obsessed about it since the morning 
With the devotion of someone who only waits for you, and the meaning you give to life itself by your mere presence

I’ll come starred with music - the new interstellar traveling of Christine and the Queens, I did it for you. In secrecy of frequencies, in genius musicians, in New York Jazz, in Moroder Groove, I kept on obsessing about this celebration, this big night found again, and I leapt into my dream. Names, boxes, they never defined what we share together. The electricity remains eternally mysterious. We’ll dream together of the blue flower, of this signal that keeps pinging from another planet that we don’t even know of yet; we’ll dream peace, peace with a common story, one way bigger than the one they taught us.

"Rendez-vous Avec Toi" comes with a music video directed by Redcar with Raphaël De Albuquerque. Check it out below along with "Rendez-vous In Your Arms."

entry.title: Kiwi Jr. – “Something Wicked”
entry.summary: Toronto indie rockers Kiwi Jr. are back with "Something Wicked," an outtake from the sessions for their recent album 'Blowin' Up.'
entry.content:
Toronto rockers Kiwi Jr. recorded their recent album Blowin' Up in Detroit with Holy Fuck's Graham Walsh, and they enlisted local Michigan artists like Stef Chura, Fred Thomas, and Protomartyr's Joe Casey and Greg Ahee to help out (alongside non-Michiganders including Alvvays' Kerri Maclellan and En Attendant Ana's Margaux Bouchaudon). Today, they're back with an outtake from those sessions, a sparkling indie-pop jam entitled "Something Wicked." Frontman Jeremy Gaudet explains:

"Something Wicked" was one of the earliest songs written for the album, and this version was recorded during the Blowin' Up sessions in Detroit. As we kept writing songs and got closer to finishing the album, the wind changed and left the song standing on it's own in terms of the feeling and ideas. It's one of our favourite songs to play, but by the time we finished the album, it just didn't fit in with the rest. The lyric is a take on some Shakespearean witches brewing up something special to steer you off course; trouble coming in all shapes and sizes from where you least expect it.

Listen below.

entry.title: Quivers – “Bottle The Nervous”
entry.summary: Melbourne indie rockers Quivers signed to Merge for 2024’s impressive Oyster Cuts. Now reconfigured into a trio, the band is back today with “Bottle The Nervous,” a subtly spectacular new song that serves as the A-side for a 7″ out this week. Propulsive yet gentle, it swept me away immediately, then charmed me with lyrics…
entry.content:
Melbourne indie rockers Quivers signed to Merge for 2024's impressive Oyster Cuts. Now reconfigured into a trio, the band is back today with "Bottle The Nervous," a subtly spectacular new song that serves as the A-side for a 7" out this week. Propulsive yet gentle, it swept me away immediately, then charmed me with lyrics like "You bottle the nervous/ It hurts so good/ Like being nervous should."

Quivers' statement provides context:

This song was written while living that dream of finally really touring our previous album, Oyster Cuts. It’s a song that partly bottles the fear and excitement of having a first kid. It’s also probably a song about other firsts: first songs you remember, first confusing friendships, the first time you saw a motorbike on fire. These are new musicians and this is a new chapter for Quivers. There’s some fear and excitement around that, too.

Listen below.

"Bottle The Nervous" b/w "Drive Somewhere" is out 11/6 on Merge. "Drive Somewhere" is physical-only, so pre-order the record here if you want to hear it.

entry.title: Crate – “Crushed To Nothing”
entry.summary: The number of Crate songs is about to expand dramatically. The Brooklyn shoegaze band made a big impact with their 2024 debut single “Julia,” which landed on our list of that year’s best shoegaze songs. But then Crate took a year to release their next single “Necklace,” and then another year and a half after…
entry.content:
The number of Crate songs is about to expand dramatically. The Brooklyn shoegaze band made a big impact with their 2024 debut single "Julia," which landed on our list of that year's best shoegaze songs. But then Crate took a year to release their next single "Necklace," and then another year and a half after that to finally announce their debut album. But now it's coming, and the Crate catalog grows by one more song today.

Crate's self-titled debut finally arrives next week. It includes "Julia," "Necklace," and "Not My Song (Mine To Keep)," the single that the band shared when they announced the LP. The record also features "Crushed To Nothing," the elegantly trippy fuzz-pedal masher that ends the album. In a press release, band member Ezra Engler says:

This one’s tricky because there’s multiple themes in this song. The main sentiment is about caring deeply about someone who is in a bad position. You do whatever you can to help them out, but you realize at the end of the day the only person that can help them is themselves. I’ve been on both sides of this coin, the helper and the helpee. This song definitely feels the most personal to me. I often write lyrics quickly and haphazardly — just kind of what I'm feeling in the moment. Then I read the lyrics back and I'm like, "Whoa, I was actually talking about something here." The outro spoken-word section switches to the thought of looking back on the past and reminiscing on things you could have done differently. Hindsight is 20/20 kinda vibe.

Listen below.

Crate is out 11/13 on Good English.

entry.title: Blue Bendy – “Vocal Fry Academia”
entry.summary: UK art-rock sextet Blue Bendy will release their sophomore album One Day This Will All Be Lore early next year, and we’ve already posted lead single “Dragonslayer.” Yesterday, the band shared “Vocal Fry Academia,” a drawling, self-aware, wordplay-heavy track that builds from an ornate ballad to a swirling hyperpop attack. The lyrics seem to concern…
entry.content:
UK art-rock sextet Blue Bendy will release their sophomore album One Day This Will All Be Lore early next year, and we've already posted lead single "Dragonslayer." Yesterday, the band shared "Vocal Fry Academia," a drawling, self-aware, wordplay-heavy track that builds from an ornate ballad to a swirling hyperpop attack. The lyrics seem to concern the fleeting nature of extremely niche fame: "Whatever happened to bendycore? Probs hit the grave seven or eight microtrends ago." Here's what lead singer Arthur Nolan says about it:

For the first time ever, started with the title (a clear albeit opaque idea) and then worked backwards. Never done it before, not sure I'll ever have the foresight to do it again. Another navel-gazing anthem that wants to have its memetic flowers and distance itself from the culture as much as possible. It’s all just isolated parasocial self-loathing and performative vanity. There’s probably a lot more where that came from. In the meantime, I think we should just all embrace the nihilistic reality of "being the best you, you can be."

Keyboardist Olivia Morgan directed the song's cryptic, cinematic video. In a press release, she says:

This video was another experiment. After making a sort of essay/collage for "Dragonslayer," I wanted to try and write more of a story for "Vocal Fry Academia" and get some friends involved to act in it. It was a lot of experimentation and learning things on the fly, and it highlighted to me how much musicians and artists rely on friendships and helping each other out to make things work. Thanks so much to everyone who was involved! Directing this many people while also shooting was terrifying but ultimately really fun and exciting. The video is sort of a homage to David Lynch, as well as a homage to the friends I got to perform in it.

Check it out below.

One Day This Will All Be Lore is out 1/29/27 on Practise Music.

entry.title: Font – “Cling”
entry.summary: The sonically adventurous Austin indie rockers Font were a Stereogum Band To Watch in 2024, and they made some very cool stylistic choices on “Texas” and “Punish Talk,” the first two singles from their upcoming LP American Bully XL. That streak continues with the new song “Cling,” a moody and synthy ballad that goes hard…
entry.content:
The sonically adventurous Austin indie rockers Font were a Stereogum Band To Watch in 2024, and they made some very cool stylistic choices on "Texas" and "Punish Talk," the first two singles from their upcoming LP American Bully XL. That streak continues with the new song "Cling," a moody and synthy ballad that goes hard on guitar sustain and gooey, underwater keyboard sounds.

The vocals are nothing alike, but "Cling" has some of the same reassuring astral drift that I hear in every Bon Iver record after For Emma, Forever Ago. Band member Anthony Laurence says, "The song is carved away from a mountain of first thoughts, recalling a subtractive process that aims to preserve ghosts, confuse source, and respond to material rather than direct it." Check it out below.

American Bully XL is out 11/13 via Acrophase.

Hover is due this coming February on Epitaph, preceded today by the lightly psychedelic pop-rock gem “Sad Songs.” The hook from Livvy Bennett is highly relatable for anyone who’s been…
entry.content:
Mamalarky do not let up. The Austin indie rockers dropped Hex Key in April 2025, and they'll have the follow-up out in under two years. Hover is due this coming February on Epitaph, preceded today by the lightly psychedelic pop-rock gem "Sad Songs." The hook from Livvy Bennett is highly relatable for anyone who's been through a breakup or some other tribulation: "Sad songs sound sadder now/ Waking up just drags me down." It's maybe not aligned with the feeling in America today after voters resoundingly rebuked Donald Trump and his dipshit enablers, but in a vacuum, it's a fantastic track. And, true to the album title, it really does seem to hover.

Bennett's statement makes me wonder if, actually, this is the perfect song for a day like today:

To me, it sounds like the first sunny day after a week-long depressive episode, the day when you remember to drink water again and find symbolism in everything but are definitely not okay yet. I hope it offers company to anyone going through loneliness, loss, and general confusion of the heart. Sometimes you’re left only with a sad song or two to make sense of some bullshit, the sole survivors of a world of hurt.

Watch the Otium-directed "Sad Songs" video below.

entry.content:
This is a great morning for some cleansing, euphoric anger, and Volcano have hit us with exactly the kind of violent music that the moment demands. This is not the band called Volcano that's got members of Sublime and the Meat Puppets, by the way. This Volcano is an Ohio band that makes brutally heavy and ignorant hardcore. Cody Davidson, from old-school death metal revivalists Sanguisugabogg plays every instrument and co-writes all the songs with tattoo-artist vocalist Jeremy Damron. This Volcano's two new songs are hitting right now.

Volcano broke in with the debut EP Fool 2 Tha Game in 2023, and they followed with the two-song single No Way Back last year. Today, they're back with another brutal two-song crusher with some characteristically gruesome cover art. Both new songs, "Lay Low" and "Salt," are galvanizing chug-mosh anthems that might make you feel like your veins are on fire. "Salt" ends with a Willie Hutch sample that I was not expecting. Hear both tracks below.

The Ear 2 Ear single is out now on DAZE.

entry.title: lots of hands – “anything for now”
entry.summary: Hear UK duo lots of hands team up with caroline guitarist Mike O'Malley on their polished new track "anything for now."
entry.content:
lots of hands are adding some more hands to the mix. Following the release of their Fire Talk debut into a pretty room early last year; the unexpected TikTok virality of their 2020 track "mistake"; US tours with Hudson Freeman, Lala Lala, and Deadharrie; and the new single "Grapevine"; the 22-year-old Newcastle-upon-Tyne duo of Billy Woodhouse and Elliot Dryden are recording in a proper studio with an outsider producer for the first time ever.

That producer is Mike O'Malley, the guitarist for fellow capitalization-averse experimentalists caroline who also worked on My New Band Believe's excellent debut. Together, they've made "anything for now," which ups the studio polish without losing any of lots of hands' usual shaggy eccentric charm. Woodhouse explains:

This song has been through about 4 stages. It started as 3 different tracks me and Elliot worked on individually, before combining them. We recorded this version down in London next to the best pastry shop we’ve ever been to. Such a luxury to have this experience, and meet Mike from caroline who really took this song to a different level.

O’Malley adds:

I was tasked with the pleasure of choosing a track to work on from a big list of really beautiful songs. "anything for now" stood out to me as a track that would be nice to work on as it had a really distinct sonic identity already, and it was a super well-written song. We built the whole thing from scratch in Park Chapel Studios in North London in one day — somewhere I always like to work because the live room sounds really good —and the engineer there, Joe, is a good friend and a talented person. It can be a really fun task taking a track that’s clearly already very developed and just exploding outwards into "studio" territory. Elliot waited patiently all day to record his vocals and did each layer in basically one take, flawlessly, right at the end of the day.

Listen to "anything for now" below.

entry.title: Shygirl – “Eternal”
entry.summary: We’re a few days away from UK club-pop experimenter Shygirl releasing new new album Swallow!, and we’ve already posted her singles “Alyse,” “Lucky (Hymn),” and “Mantra.” Yesterday, Shygirl shared one more advance single, and it’s the final track on the album. “Eternal” is a spacey, pretty track that recalls the more psychedelic variations on trip-hop…
entry.content:
We're a few days away from UK club-pop experimenter Shygirl releasing new new album Swallow!, and we've already posted her singles "Alyse," "Lucky (Hymn)," and "Mantra." Yesterday, Shygirl shared one more advance single, and it's the final track on the album. "Eternal" is a spacey, pretty track that recalls the more psychedelic variations on trip-hop that showed up in a lot of car commercials around the end of the '90s. I mean that in the good way.

Shygirl co-produced "Eternal" with Casey MQ, Dahi, Ely Rise, and Karma Kid. It's a woozy, pretty cascade of breakbeats, strings, and floaty upper-register vocals, and it moves away from the more anthemic dance stuff that Shygirl often makes. Along with the track, Shygirl has unveiled plans for a spring tour that'll take her across North America and Europe. Check out "Eternal" and those dates below.

entry.title: Liars – “Beat Creep Some Eyes”
entry.summary: This is proving to be a rough morning for lowercase-letter liars, but it’s looking a lot better for capital-letter Liars. Next year, the band, now a solo project for longtime frontman Angus Andrew, will release A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans, a new album inspired by the time that Andrew and his family spent in…
entry.content:
This is proving to be a rough morning for lowercase-letter liars, but it's looking a lot better for capital-letter Liars. Next year, the band, now a solo project for longtime frontman Angus Andrew, will release A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans, a new album inspired by the time that Andrew and his family spent in Kalamazoo, Michigan. (Good morning for Michigan, by the way.) We've already heard the lead single "Ice Pick, Kalamazoo," and now Andrew has also shared a new song called "Beat Creep Some Eyes."

"Beat Creep Some Eyes" is a hypnotic track driven by sustained synth drones and rolling-freakout drums. Angus Andrew's voice, a drawn-out deadpan chant, sounds otherworldly. Clemens Habicht put together the evocative video using black-and-white photos that Andrew took with a 3D camera around Kalamazoo. Both song and video capture a feeling of creeping decay. Here's what Andrew says about it:

Sometimes, I think the strangest thing isn't that the world is absurd, but how quickly we get used to it. You can find yourself living inside something completely ridiculous, and after a while it just becomes Tuesday. Then you start to wonder if you're seeing things clearly at all. You know what you're looking at, but you're no longer sure you're seeing it correctly. I think the music lives somewhere in that space.

Check it out below.

A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans is out 3/5 on Mute.

entry.content:
Dutch Uncles aren't actually Dutch; they're from Manchester. No word on whether they're actually uncles, though. I bet at least some of them are uncles. The zippy art-pop band has six members; there's got to be at least two uncles in there. We last heard from Dutch Uncles when they released the 2023 album True Entertainment, and frontuncle Robin Richards dropped his solo debut Taproots last year. (Richards is actually the bassist and lead composer, and I'm not sure if that makes him the bandleader or not. Just couldn't resist the word "frontuncle.") Now, there's a new Dutch Uncs record on the way.

Early next year, Dutch Uncles will release Polygon Hotel, the new album that they produced themselves, with Geese/Lime Hotel collaborator Felix Davis on hand to mix it. It's their first since becoming a sextet, with longtime collaborators Henry Broadhead, a multi-instrumentalist, and Neil Wright, a guitarist, as full members of the band.

Lead single "No Note" has a bit of the classic XTC or Tears For Fears gene. It's this big, busy song with an elaborate arrangement and a whole lot of marimba, and its melodic decisions veer all over the place. In a press release, Duncan Wallis, the band member who could perhaps be best described as frontuncle, says this:

A three-minute lament on time wasted looking at one’s phone. Specifically, time spent on social media and a regret that so much of our lives has been invested into the engine of social media, just for it to be snatched up and controlled by the worst people imaginable.

And, somewhat ironically considering it’s a reflection on time wasted, it only took five minutes to write the lyrics.

Patrick King directed the "No Note" video, and Miles Buckle did the nightmarish '90s-style CGI animation. Check it out below, along with the Polygon Hotel tracklist and Dutch Uncles' upcoming tour dates.

entry.title: Anna McClellan – “Anywhere” (Feat. Gloorp)
entry.summary: Folk-rock singer-songwriter shares "Anywhere," a collaboration with Philadelphia producer Gloorp off of her upcoming EP 'South Of Dodge.'
entry.content:
Fresh off of singing backup on Greg Freeman's new album All Set The Bone and dropping her own EP Space, you big cloud, folk-rock singer-songwriter Anna McClellan is capping off a busy year with the release of another EP. South Of Dodge, named after a street in McClellan's native Omaha, is out later this month, and she's already shared early track "Drank Earlier." Now we're getting "Anywhere," a collaboration with Garrett Burke, the Philly producer and percussionist known as Gloorp. McClellan explains:

"Anywhere" is about impending change, which makes sense because I wrote it right before I moved from Omaha. You know when you’re supposed to be packing but you just sit at your piano and write a song instead. I was falling in love. I was hanging out with new people. It felt fresh, it felt like a scene was emerging that I had written off as impossible. I was like, of course, things always start to line up right before you leave, making the exit much more bittersweet than you imagined 6 months ago. It literally ALWAYS happens. I’m pretty sure it's Newton’s fourth law? “An object about to be in motion must second guess everything.”

Huge shoutout to Garrett Burke aka Gloorp for the beat!!! I just asked him to make a sick beat and he was like, ok I got you. If only it was always this easy. Love you Garrett.

Hear the surprisingly winningly combination of McClellan's intimate Americana and Gloorp's clattering electronic beats below.

The South Of Dodge EP is out 11/20 on Exploding In Sound.

entry.title: Kora Puckett – “In My Veins”
entry.summary: Narrow Head guitarist Kora Puckett has signed to TODO Records and shared a new country-rock solo single called "In My Veins."
entry.content:
Kora Puckett, the Narrow Head guitarist who's also played with bands including the Berries, Sheer Mag, and Angel Du$t, is stepping out on his own. The Indiana-born, Los Angeles-based musician, who debuted with a three-song EP back in 2024, has officially signed to TODO Records, and he's announcing the news with a brand new single.

While Puckett is mostly known for his work with bands on the harder end of the alt-rock spectrum, his solo stuff is country-tinged indie rock, a sound that's on full display on "In My Veins." Puckett says that the track "was the start of a new ethos for me with music - keep things loose and open, surround yourself with artists who you love that you can lean on."

The accompanying music video from director Justice Vaughn Ott captures the song's easygoing charms with footage of Puckett wandering around Los Angeles, looking through records, playing with a dog, and strumming his guitar on a front porch. Check it out below, and watch out for his debut solo album arriving sometime in 2027.

Must be nice. 1000 Rabbits is a lot of rabbits, and it’s also the name of the buzzy London-based post-punk band that…
entry.content:
Seems like most of the acts releasing new music today don't come from the United States. It's like they don't have some monumentally important election hanging over their heads on this particular Tuesday. Must be nice.

1000 Rabbits is a lot of rabbits, and it's also the name of the buzzy London-based post-punk band that already impressed us with the singles "Virgin Soil" and "Rubik's Cube." They're young and they're on the label known as Young. Old people note: Their new song "Stupid Boy" has nothing to do with Garbage's "Stupid Girl." Instead, it's a tangled, idiosyncratic number that starts out quiet and builds to a raging conclusion. The crescendos really hit, especially when the violin gets involved. Here's what the band says about it:

This summer, we’ve had a wild time in Europe and the UK playing at festivals and touring our EP. The song became a space to experiment with lots of facets of our performance — singing all together, getting into the crowd, dancing and shouting: things we’d never done before but that the song demanded. It’s cathartic, and sharing that feeling with an audience and seeing it resonate has been magical. It’s one of our wildest, angriest, most cathartic experiments so far, and we are proud of its volatile constitution — it could explode at any moment

Check out the Cuan Roche-directed video below.

"Stupid Boy" is out now on Young.

entry.content:
Belgian art-pop artists Charlotte Adigéry and Bolis Pupul first worked together on Adigéry's self-titled debut EP in 2017, and they teamed up for the collaborative album Topical Dancer in 2022. Now, they're doing it again. After releasing a single called "Googoo Gaga" last month, Adigéry and Pupul will release their second LP as a duo early next year. It's called Mainland Madinina.

Adigéry and Pupul wrote Mainland Madinina together in Ghent and Martinique, the homeland of Adigéry's mother. (Madinina is the indigenous name for Martinique.) It's the first thing that the two artists recorded after they both became parents and Adigéry lost her mother. Soulwax acted as mentors and co-producers for the record, just as they did on Topical Dancer.

Adigéry and Pupul's new single "From Healer To Dealer" is a twitchy, funky dance-pop track that goes on for eight and a half minutes and concerns two narcissistic characters who speak to each other entirely in buzzwords. Lennert Madou directed the video, and it stars dancers Emmanuelle Mfulu and Mathias Goethals. Below, check out that clip, the Mainland Madinina tracklist, and Adigéry and Pupul's upcoming tour dates.
